---
title: "In-memory"
---

The `from_*` and `register_*` methods upload an **in-memory frame** (pandas, polars, Arrow, or plain Python) directly into your `Workspace`. Each one uploads the rows, creates a source table, and returns the table's `DataFrame`.

The same upload can be done in two ways:

- `from_*` — `table_name` is optional; a name is auto-generated if you omit it.
- `register_*` — `table_name` is required and positional.

```python
import pandas as pd

df = pd.DataFrame({"id": [1, 2, 3], "region": ["us", "eu", "us"]})

# Optional name (auto-generated if omitted)
op_df = ws.from_pandas(df)
op_df = ws.from_pandas(df, table_name="regions")

# Explicit name (required, positional)
op_df = ws.register_pandas(df, "regions")
```

Pick the method that matches your object:

| Object | `from_*` (name optional) | `register_*` (name required) |
| :-- | :-- | :-- |
| pandas | `from_pandas(df, table_name=…)` | `register_pandas(df, "name")` |
| polars | `from_polars(df, table_name=…)` | `register_polars(df, "name")` |
| Arrow `Table` / `RecordBatch` | `from_arrow(tbl, table_name=…)` | `register_arrow(tbl, "name")` |
| list of dicts | `from_pylist(rows, table_name=…)` | `register_pylist(rows, "name")` |
| dict of columns | `from_pydict(cols, table_name=…)` | `register_pydict(cols, "name")` |
